 JUDGMENT
This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- in respect of accidental injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. In the petition it is stated that on 26.08.2021 petitioner was going towards his village R.Gadduru from K.Bypalli by riding TVS Jupiter bearing reg.No.KA-08-W-4691 by observing traffic rules at 7.00 pm when he reached near Shettikal Keshavachari's house, Mylapura road Mulbagal Taluk,
Srinivasareddy vs B. Srinivasareddy on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14583594/

Kolar District, one Eicher goods Tempo bearing reg.No.KA-53-C-2124 which was going ahead of petitioner's scooter, suddenly stopped without giving any indication in the middle of the road due to which, petitioner who was behind the said vehicle hit the same and caused accident.
The petitioner tried to avoid the collision but he could not control as there was no signal or indication and also due to light emitted by opposite coming vehicles.
Due to this impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
That he was admitted to R.L.Jalappa hospital, Kolar and found that he sustained Grade IV liver injury, fracture shaft of left femur, fracture 8th right side rib, superior pulmonary venous thrombosis.
He was treated as inpatient and underwent surgery.
He was discharged from the hospital on 09.10.2021.
He was an Agriculturist and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the accident he lost the income.
He is unable to work as (SCCH-12) 3 MVC.No.5836/2021 earlier.
He has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards treatment, medicine etc.
The accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Goods Tempo bearing reg.No.KA-53-C- 2124.
The 1st respondent is the owner and 2nd respondent is the insurer and they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
On all these grounds he prayed to allow the petition and award compensation along with interest and costs in the above case.
3. On issuance of notice to the respondent no.1 and 2 they appeared through their respective counsel and have filed written statement separately.
4. Respondent No.1 owner filed written statement contending that petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
He denied the accident and manner of accident alleged by the petitioner.
He stated that the vehicle bearing reg. No.KA-53-C- 2124 is duly insured with 2 nd respondent.
The injuries alleged by the petitioner are false.
The driver of Goods vehicle was driving it in slow speed by observing traffic rules on correct side of the road.

The petitioner was riding his vehicle at high speed by talking in mobile phone and without observing the vehicles moving in front of his vehicle,
dashed to the tempo to its back side as such, the accident is due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself and therefore, this respondent is not liable to pay compensation.
Medical treatment and expenses alleged are denied.
Age, occupation and income of the petitioner are denied.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the petition.
2nd respondent insurance company filed written statement contending that petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Age, occupation and income of the petitioner are denied.
Disability of the petitioner and the manner of accident alleged in the petition are denied.
That driver of tempo was not holding valid driving licence as on the date of accident.
That petitioner was not maintaining healthy distance from the tempo and he was riding his scooter by taking in mobile due to which, he hit the tempo and caused accident.
There is no negligence on part of tempo driver.
The compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of IMV Act are disputed.
Therefore, this respondent is not liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
He sought permission to contest the petition under Section 170 of IMV Act.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessors-in office has framed the following:-

sentences.text: ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that the injuries shown in petition are sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 26.08.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Eicher Goods Tempo bearing No.KA-53-C-2124 which hit petitioner's TVS Jupiter bearing No.KA-08-W- 4691?
2. Whether the petitioner prove his age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any?
3. Whether respondent no.2 Insurance company proves that the driver of Tempo was not (SCCH-12) 5 MVC.No.5836/2021 possessing valid and effective DL as on the date of accident?
4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so by whom and what is the quantum?
5. What Order or Award?
7. To prove his case, petitioner is examined as P.W.1.
Ex.P.1 to P.9 documents are marked on his behalf.
Doctor by name Nagakumar, Professor in the Department of R.L.Jalappa hospital, Kolar is examined as P.W.2 and through him Ex.P.10 to 15 documents are marked.
On respondent side Assistant Manager of 2nd respondent insurance company is examined as R.W.1.

Through him Ex.R.1 to R.5 documents are marked and respondent evidence is closed.
8.
Heard learned counsel for both sides and perused records.
Respondent no.2 filed written arguments.

Counsel for petitioner has relied on the points in following decisions:
1) Divisional Controller, MSRTC V/s Bismilah and Others 2024 ACJ 173, High Court of Karnataka, Dharwad Bench 2) Lachoo Ram and Others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation (2014) 13 SCC 254 9.

On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
Issue No.1: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3: In the Negative, Issue No.4: Partly in the Affirmative, (SCCH-12) 6 MVC.No.5836/2021 Issue No.5: As per final order, for the following;

ISSUE NO.1: To prove that petitioner sustained injuries due to RTA on 26.08.2021 at 7.00 pm by rash and negligent driving of the driver of Goods Tempo bearing No.KA-53-C-2124, petitioner entered into the witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
He reiterated petition averments in his chief examination.
The MLC extract and police intimation are not produced in the above case.

FIR produced at Ex.P.1 shows that one Dhananjaya Reddy has given first information to Nangali police station stating that his cousin Srinivasa reddy was riding his two wheeler on 26.08.2021 on Mylapura K.Bypalli road near Shettikal Keshavachari's house, at that time, driver of one Goods Tempo bearing No.KA-53-C-2124 who was going in front of Srinivasa Reddy's scooter stopped the vehicle without giving signal, due to which Srinivasa Reddy hit behind the tempo and sustained grievous injuries.

That he was shifted to R.L Jalappa, Kolar and from there to Manipal hospital,
Bengaluru and then again to R.L. Jalappa hospital, Kolar and he is undergoing treatment, therefore action may be taken against the driver of Eicher Goods vehicle.

11. On receiving this first information on 27.08.2021 i.e. on the next day of accident, Nangali police station registered Crime No.111/2021 against the driver of Eicher vehicle for the offence p/u/s 279,337, of IPC.
Spot panchanama was drawn on same day of the FIR and it is mentioned in the panchanama, that first informant has shown the spot.
It is 16 ft wide tar road.
The (SCCH-12) 7 MVC.No.5836/2021 accident took place on the left side of the road.
Both the vehicles were found at the spot.
As per the IMV report rear safety bar of the tempo got damaged and head light assembly of the scooter got damaged.
The wound certificate produced at Ex.P.5 shows the history of skid and fall from two wheeler on 26.08.2021 around 7.30pm.
As per the wound certificate petitioner sustained 6 injuries out of which, 3 are grievous and 3 are simple in nature.
After investigation charge sheet is filed against the driver of tempo for the offence p/u/s 279, 337 and 338 of IPC stating that he was driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner.

In the discharge summary produced at Ex.P.7 also it is mentioned as two wheeler skid and fall and petitioner was brought from Manipal hospital on 27.08.2021.
12.
The 1st respondent though filed written statement has not cross examined P.W.1, on the contention that petitioner was riding motor cycle by talking over mobile phone.
Therefore, 1 st respondent has not proved the said fact.
The 2 nd respondent cross examined P.W.1 at length.
He questioned about driving licence of the petitioner.
Petitioner stated that he lost the driving licence and has not given complainant regarding the same.
Though this question is asked, it is necessary to mention that, the petitioner not having driving licence will not be fundamental breach of contract to affect the liability of the insurance company.
Hence the said suggestion is not material to decide the case on hand.
Further the petitioner stated that he was going in 20km speed per hour and denied that he could have stopped the vehicle in such speed.
The suggestion that (SCCH-12) 8 MVC.No.5836/2021 opponent vehicle is falsely implicated in the case is denied.
He stated that he fell on the left side of the road.
The suggestion that his right rib got fractured, but he fell on left side of the road and he has given false case all are denied.
The suggestion that vehicle belonging to his own villager is implicated in the case is denied.
13. It is necessary to notice that on the basis of this evidence, it can be seen that as per the wound certificate petitioner sustained skid and fall on 26.08.2024.
MLC extract and police intimation sent to the concerned police are not produced before the court.

There is no mention as to whether there Srinivasareddy vs B. Srinivasareddy on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14583594/
4 was MLC maintained and sent to police or not.

sentences.text: Even as per discharge summary also petitioner sustained skid and fall.
There is delay of one day in filing the first information.
In the complaint it is stated that, petitioner was undergoing treatment.
2nd respondent contended that opponent vehicle has been falsely implicated in the case only to claim compensation.
The said fact is denied by the P.W.1.
There is no sketch drawn by the concerned police to show how the accident took place or to show the place of the accident.
14. According to petitioner, aforesaid tempo was involved in the accident.

To prove this contention,
petitioner produced FIR and Final report in which involvement of this vehicle is shown coupled with his oral evidence.
But as per 2 nd respondent, this vehicle was falsely implicated in the case.
Since 2 nd respondent contended that this vehicle was not involved in the case, he could have examined witnesses to prove his contention and disprove the contents of final report.
No eye witness are (SCCH-12) 9 MVC.No.5836/2021 examined to show that opponent vehicle was not involved in the matter.
Driver and owner of the vehicle have not questioned the final report or first information.
Hence this contention of the 2 nd respondent has not been proved.
15. In respect of negligence, in the first information as well as in the oral evidence petitioner stated that driver of opponent vehicle suddenly stopped the vehicle without giving any indication.
It is necessary to notice that if the petitioner has maintained safe distance between his vehicle and opponent vehicle he could have stopped his vehicle from hitting the same.
Further, it is stated that petitioner could not see the front side vehicle due to emitting lights of the opposite side coming vehicle.

If he could not see the vehicle due to the lights, immediately stopped the could have stopped the vehicle or slowed down his vehicle, and allow the opposite coming vehicles to pass and emitting light to pass away, but he proceeded without maintaining safe distance.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court there is some contribution of petitioner himself to the accident.
Though involvement of 2nd respondent vehicle is disputed the FIR and final report are not questioned by owner or the driver of the opponent vehicle.
The fact that tempo driver stopped the vehicle without giving any indication is not denied by the driver nor disputed by the 1st respondent by cross examining P.W.1 or giving his own evidence.
Therefore, it is clear that, the driver of opponent vehicle also contributed to the accident.

The statement that petitioner was talking over phone and hit behind the tempo gives an indication that tempo was (SCCH-12) 10 MVC.No.5836/2021 present at the spot and according to owner it is petitioner himself came and hit the tempo.
But, to prove this fact, he has not appeared before the court to give evidence.
Though it is mentioned as skid and fall how petitioner fell down has been proved by petitioner by showing driver of opponent vehicle suddenly stopped the vehicle.
In that view of the matter I am of the opinion that, contribution of the petitioner to the accident is 20% and contribution of tempo driver is 80% in the above case.
Accordingly, I hold Issue No.1 Partly in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE NO.2 :
In respect of age, petitioner produced his aadhaar card at Ex.P8 which shows that he was born on 01.01.1988.
Accident took place on 26.08.2021.
Respondent no.2 disputed the age of the petitioner.
He was aged 33 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner is considered as 33 years at the time of accident.

sentences.text: In respect of occupation it is stated that, petitioner was an Agriculturist and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
To prove his earnings petitioner has not produced any document.

Hence,
notional income has to be considered Rs.15,000/- per month and same is considered as his monthly income.
18. In respect of permanent disability a doctor by name Naga Kumar, Professor in Dept of Orthopedics, R.L.Jalappa hospital, Kolar is examined as P.W.2.

entities.text: Dept of Orthopedics, R.L.Jalappa hospital, Kolar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In his chief examination he stated that petitioner has sustained Grade IV liver injury, fracture shaft of left femur, fracture of 8th right side rib, superior pulmonary venous thromboisis.
Surgery was conducted in the form of ORIF with IMIL nailing for left femur fracture on (SCCH-12) 11 MVC.No.5836/2021 29.09.2021 and other injuries were treated conservatively.
P.W.2 has assessed physical disability of 41.86% of left lower limb and 13.9% of whole body.

Radiological examination revealed fractures of left femur AP &
lateral shows implants in situ, fracture site shows callus, satisfactory reduction.
19. In the cross examination it is suggested that, at the time of discharge, petitioner was healthy.
P.W.2 admitted the same.
The suggestion that petitioner can work as agriculturist is denied.
As per the evidence of doctor petitioner has whole body disability of 13.9%.
Considering the occupation of the petitioner, the disability in left lower limb will affect his income therefore there is functional disability which affects the income of the petitioner.
In the opinion of this court the disability of 41.86% in the left lower limb affects the income of the petitioner at 12%.
Accordingly functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner is held as 12%.
Accordingly, I answer this issue Partly in the Affirmative.
20. ISSUE NO.3 :
2nd respondent insurance company contended that driver of Tempo was not holding valid and effective driving license.
To prove this fact no satisfactory evidence is placed before the court.
Charge sheet does not show any such charge on the driver or owner.
No notice is issued to the driver to produce his driving licence.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court this issue is not proved by the 2 nd respondent.
Accordingly, Issue No.3 is answered in the "Negative".
21. ISSUE NO.4 :
In view of above reasons, injuries sustained by petitioner are due to the accident caused by the driver of the (SCCH-12) 12 MVC.No.5836/2021 Goods Tempo bearing No.KA-53-C-2124.
There is nexus between the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the accident.
Hence, he is entitled to compensation at the hands of respondents.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.8.
Totally he has paid amount of Rs.3,15,296/- as per Ex.P.8 medical bills.
The said payment of bill is due to the accident caused to him.
They are subsequent to the date of accident.
Though they are disputed, no satisfactory material is placed to disbelieve the bills.
They are supported by prescriptions of the doctor.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.3,15,296/-.
(ii) Food and nourishment:

The petitioner was admitted in R.L.Jalappa hospital from 27.08.2021 and discharge on 24.09.2021 and has produced discharge summaries at Srinivasareddy vs B. Srinivasareddy on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14583594/
6 Ex.P.7.
Further he was again admitted on 24.09.2021 and discharged on 09.10.2021.
He was in hospital for almost 44 days.
Accident took place in the year 2021.
Since he was in hospital, food and nourishment charges will have to be awarded.
Considering the cost of living, and food, nourishment charges if per day Rs.300/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for food and nourishment Rs.300/- x 44 days = Rs.13,200/-is awarded.
(iii) Attendant charges:
For a period of inpatient for 44 days some one should have looked after petitioner in the hospital.
Even if his family member has taken care of him in the said (SCCH-12) 13 MVC.No.5836/2021 period, that family member's income for those days is lost.
Hence per day if Rs.300/- is awarded as attendant charges in 2021, it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for attendant charges Rs.300/- x 44 days =Rs.13,200/-is awarded.
(iv) Loss of income during laid up period:
As per the finding to issue No.2, the income of the petitioner per month is Rs.15,000/-.
He suffered 6 injuries out of which 3 injuries are grievous and 3 injuries are simple in nature.
He was inpatient for 44 days and he was advised to take rest.
Minimum 6 months is required to recover from such grievous injury.
Therefore, laid up period of petitioner is considered as total 6 months including in patient period and loss of income during laid up period is Rs.15,000/-x 6= Rs. 90,000/-
He is entitled to Rs.90,000/- as loss of income during laid up period.
(v) Conveyance charges:
It is stated that petitioner took treatment at RL Jalappa hospital and Manipal hospital.
He has spent money for conveyance for the purpose of treatment.

Hence,
conveyance charges of Rs.5,000/- is awarded.
(vi) Loss of future income due to Disability :
As per the findings given to issue no.2, there is functional disability of 12%.
Therefore, loss of future income due to disability is to be calculated as income per month Rs.15,000 X 12 months X 12% disability X appropriate multiplier to the age group of 31-35 is 16.
Hence, in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.3,45,600/- towards loss of future income due to disability.
For Future medical expenses:
P.W.2 doctor who has assessed the disability of the petitioner has stated that petitioner needs to removal the implants which may require Rs.25-30,000/- but no estimation is produced.
In view of necessity of removal of implants for well being of the petitioner in the opinion of this court amount of Rs.25,000/- shall be awarded for future medical treatment.

Accordingly, Rs.25,000/-
is awarded under this head.

7 (viii) For Pain and sufferings:

sentences.text: The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries as per the wound certificate produced by him.
The records show that he underwent operation.
He was in hospital for 44 days and he underwent surgery therefore, he sustained pain and sufferings.
For pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- .
(ix) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life :

As per the evidence of treated doctor,
petitioner complained about difficulty in waling on slope, climbing stairs, standing on affected legs,
squatting, sitting cross legs, difficulty in kneeling and take turns also, he cannot walk fast and run.
He suffers discomfort.
Meaning, he cannot lead the normal life as he used to live before the accident.
Certainly accident has caused physical discomfort and come in the way of normal enjoyment of life.
Hence in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled to compensation under the head of physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life.
Under the said head he is entitled for Rs.30,000/-
(x) Loss of future prospect:

As per the evidence of assessed doctor, petitioner complained about pain and restriction in (SCCH-12) 15 MVC.No.5836/2021 movement but there is no specific evidence regarding future prospects loss of the petitioner.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:-

sentences.text: Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.7,09,837/- in respect of injuries sustained (SCCH-12) 16 MVC.No.5836/2021 by him in the Road traffic accident.

Accordingly, I answer this Issue "Partly in Affirmative".
22. ISSUE NO.6:-
In view of above reasons petitioner is entitled to compensation from the hands of Respondents.

Since 2nd respondent admitted the insurance policy valid as on the date of accident,
he is liable to indemnify the insured and pay compensation to the petitioner to the tune of Rs.7,09,837/- with interest @ of 6% from the date of petition till the date of payment excluding future medical expenses.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass following :
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,09,837/- with interest @ 6% pa on the amount of Rs.6,84,837/- from the date of petition till the date of payment.
(Future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/- will not carry interest).
The respondent no.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within 2 months from the date of this order.

The petitioner is entitled to have release of 70% compensation and remaining 30%
shall (SCCH-12) 17 MVC.No.5836/2021 be kept in F.D in the name of petitioner in any nationalized bank of his choice with a liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.

dashed to the tempo to its back side as such, the accident is due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself and therefore, this respondent is not liable to pay compensation.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the petition.
2nd respondent insurance company filed written statement contending that petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Disability of the petitioner and the manner of accident alleged in the petition are denied.
That driver of tempo was not holding valid driving licence as on the date of accident.
That petitioner was not maintaining healthy distance from the tempo and he was riding his scooter by taking in mobile due to which, he hit the tempo and caused accident.
There is no negligence on part of tempo driver.
The compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of IMV Act are disputed.
Therefore, this respondent is not liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
He sought permission to contest the petition under Section 170 of IMV Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that the injuries shown in petition are sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 26.08.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Eicher Goods Tempo bearing No.KA-53-C-2124 which hit petitioner's TVS Jupiter bearing No.KA-08-W- 4691?
2. Whether the petitioner prove his age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any?
3. Whether respondent no.2 Insurance company proves that the driver of Tempo was not (SCCH-12) 5 MVC.No.5836/2021 possessing valid and effective DL as on the date of accident?
4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so by whom and what is the quantum?
5. What Order or Award?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Counsel for petitioner has relied on the points in following decisions:
1) Divisional Controller, MSRTC V/s Bismilah and Others 2024 ACJ 173, High Court of Karnataka, Dharwad Bench 2) Lachoo Ram and Others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation (2014) 13 SCC 254 9.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Since 2 nd respondent contended that this vehicle was not involved in the case, he could have examined witnesses to prove his contention and disprove the contents of final report.
No eye witness are (SCCH-12) 9 MVC.No.5836/2021 examined to show that opponent vehicle was not involved in the matter.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court there is some contribution of petitioner himself to the accident.
Though involvement of 2nd respondent vehicle is disputed the FIR and final report are not questioned by owner or the driver of the opponent vehicle.
The fact that tempo driver stopped the vehicle without giving any indication is not denied by the driver nor disputed by the 1st respondent by cross examining P.W.1 or giving his own evidence.
Therefore, it is clear that, the driver of opponent vehicle also contributed to the accident.
There is nexus between the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the accident.
Hence, he is entitled to compensation at the hands of respondents.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries as per the wound certificate produced by him.
He was in hospital for 44 days and he underwent surgery therefore, he sustained pain and sufferings.
Meaning, he cannot lead the normal life as he used to live before the accident.
Hence in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled to compensation under the head of physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life.

In view of above reasons petitioner is entitled to compensation from the hands of Respondents.
Since 2nd respondent admitted the insurance policy valid as on the date of accident,
he is liable to indemnify the insured and pay compensation to the petitioner to the tune of Rs.7,09,837/- with interest @ of 6% from the date of petition till the date of payment excluding future medical expenses.
Accordingly, I proceed to pass following :
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,09,837/- with interest @ 6% pa on the amount of Rs.6,84,837/- from the date of petition till the date of payment.

The respondent no.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within 2 months from the date of this order.
The petitioner is entitled to have release of 70% compensation and remaining 30%
shall (SCCH-12) 17 MVC.No.5836/2021 be kept in F.D in the name of petitioner in any nationalized bank of his choice with a liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.
